items.review_rationale: Read proper-subset definition with both non-strict inclusion and strict inequality; the extra witness of an element in B outside A is required, not optional.

references.phrase: strict inequality A not equal B
references.context: Two sets have different members and are not equal; coupled to non-strict inclusion.

references.phrase: element of B not in A
references.context: An existential witness to strict inclusion, equivalently nonemptiness of B minus A.

references.disposition: Unlike the ordinary subset relation, A and B cannot be identical under this condition.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed general subspace topology from intersections of ambient open sets with arbitrary subset, including empty subset and the resulting induced topological space.

references.context: Set-theoretic intersection of subset A with ambient open subset U of X.
Collection of all intersections A cap U as U ranges over tau, with resulting topology on A.

references.disposition: General topological-space convention admits an empty subspace and does not impose a nonempty hypothesis.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed restricted topology convention under which only nonempty subsets may be topological subspaces; kept identical induced-open-set construction but not the unrestricted empty case.

references.context: An underlying subset A for which at least one element exists; source convention excludes the empty set.
Intersection of A with each open U from the ambient topology tau.
The collection of all sets A cap U for U in tau, defining the open sets on A.

references.phrase: exclusion of empty A by convention
references.disposition: This is a restricted convention, not an assertion that the general subspace topology cannot be defined on the empty set.

items.review_rationale: Read full tagged Riemann-sum epsilon–delta definition for bounded real function on nondegenerate compact interval, with arbitrary tags, finite partitions, mesh, and uniform fine-partition quantification.

references.phrase: bounded real function f:[a,b] to R
real endpoints a,b and integral L
positive integer number of subintervals n

references.context: Closed bounded real interval with strict ordering of its endpoints.
Existence of uniform bound on magnitude |f(x)| over all x in [a,b].
Finite strictly increasing endpoint subdivision of [a,b].
A freely chosen sample point in each closed subinterval of the partition.
Finite sum of values f(xi_i) times widths x_i-x_(i-1).
Maximum among lengths of the finitely many subintervals of the partition.
For every positive epsilon there exists a positive delta for which all tagged partitions of mesh below delta have sum within epsilon of L.

references.disposition: Definition is restricted to bounded integrand on compact interval with a<b, not an infinite-endpoint or singular improper integral.
